AtomicFileWrite.swift:19 writes the full payload with Data.write(.atomic), and the 0o600 chmod only runs afterwards at :20-24, so the doc comment at :8-12 overstates what it does. The attack as written still does not hold up. (1) It only works through the Codex write-back at FileCredentialReader.swift:74, which runs only when manage_oauth_refresh is true. That setting is off by default for both the struct and the decoder (AppConfig.swift:309/326 and 350/364). The finding lists this as a precondition, so the claim depends on a non-default configuration. (2) Every other 0o600 caller writes into the app's own Application Support or Caches directories. The finding itself says those are forced to 0700, so another local user cannot even see the temp file there. That covers ConfigLoader.swift:110/189/276, DiskCache.swift:135/152, UsageHistoryStore.swift:152 and OpenAIResetJournal.swift:30. (3) The window only opens if Foundation's atomic write leaves the file at 0666&~umask rather than 0600. That code is closed-source Foundation and I could not confirm it by reading anything in this repo. It also needs a second local OS user who can traverse ~/.codex. What remains is a hardening gap: an opt-in setting on a multi-user Mac, plus unverified framework behaviour. That does not meet the standard of a complete attack path with no mitigation in the default deployment. The fix is still worth doing: use open(O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW, 0o600) and fchmod before writing.
